sentences.en: There was once a house that was overrun with Mice.
sentences.zh: 从前有一所房子，老鼠成群，闹得厉害。

sentences.en: A Cat heard of this, and said to herself, "That's the place for me," and off she went and took up her quarters in the house …
sentences.zh: 一只猫听说此事，自言自语道：「那正是我该去的地方。」于是她就去了，在那所房子里安顿下来……

sentences.en: … and caught the Mice one by one and ate them.
sentences.zh: ……把老鼠一只一只抓住吃掉。

sentences.en: At last the Mice could stand it no longer, and they determined to take to their holes and stay there.
sentences.zh: 到最后老鼠们再也受不了了，决定钻进洞里不再出来。

sentences.en: "That's awkward," said the Cat to herself: "the only thing to do is to coax them out by a trick."
sentences.zh: 「这就难办了，」猫自言自语，「唯一的办法是用计策把它们引出来。」

sentences.en: So she considered a while, and then climbed up the wall and let herself hang down by her hind legs from a peg, and pretended to be dead.
sentences.zh: 她想了一会儿，然后爬上墙，用后腿挂在一根木钉上倒吊着，装死。

sentences.en: By and by a Mouse peeped out and saw the Cat hanging there.
sentences.zh: 不久，一只老鼠探出头来，看见猫吊在那里。

sentences.en: "Aha!" it cried, "you're very clever, madam, no doubt …
sentences.zh: 「啊哈！」它叫道，「夫人，您确实很聪明……」

sentences.en: … but you may turn yourself into a bag of meal hanging there, if you like, yet you won't catch us coming anywhere near you."
sentences.zh: 「……可是就算您愿意把自己变成一袋面粉挂在那儿，也休想让我们靠近你一步。」

sentences.en: If you are wise you won't be deceived by the innocent airs of those whom you have once found to be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 聪明人不会被那些一旦被识破危险就装出无辜模样的家伙骗到。

sentences.en: Once upon a time all the Mice met together in Council, and discussed the best means of securing themselves against the attacks of the cat.
sentences.zh: 有一次，所有的老鼠聚在一起开会，讨论用什么办法最好，能保自己不受猫的袭击。

sentences.en: After several suggestions had been debated, a Mouse of some standing and experience got up and said, "I think I have hit upon a plan …
sentences.zh: 议论过几个提议之后，一只颇有地位和经验的老鼠站起来说：「我想出了一个办法……」

sentences.en: … which will ensure our safety in the future, provided you approve and carry it out.
sentences.zh: 「……只要你们赞成并照办，就能保证我们今后的安全。」

sentences.en: It is that we should fasten a bell round the neck of our enemy the cat, which will by its tinkling warn us of her approach."
sentences.zh: 「那就是在我们的敌人猫的脖子上系一只铃铛，铃声一响就能提醒我们她来了。」

sentences.en: This proposal was warmly applauded, and it had been already decided to adopt it …
sentences.zh: 这个提议受到热烈鼓掌，大家已经决定采纳……

sentences.en: … when an old Mouse got upon his feet and said, "I agree with you all that the plan before us is an admirable one …
sentences.zh: ……这时一只年迈的老鼠站起来说：「我同意各位的看法，眼前这个计策确实妙……」

sentences.en: … but may I ask who is going to bell the cat?"
sentences.zh: 「……可是我想请教一句：谁去给猫系铃铛呢？」

title: The Old Woman and the Doctor
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Old Woman became almost totally blind from a disease of the eyes, and, after consulting a Doctor, made an agreement with him in the …
sentences.zh: 一位老妇因眼疾几乎完全失明。她请教过一位医生后，当着见证人的面与他立下约定：

sentences.en: … presence of witnesses that she should pay him a high fee if he cured her, while if he failed he was to receive nothing.
sentences.zh: ……若治好，她付他一笔丰厚的酬金；若治不好，他分文不取。

sentences.en: The Doctor accordingly prescribed a course of treatment …
sentences.zh: 医生于是开了一套疗程……

sentences.en: … and every time he paid her a visit he took away with him some article out of the house, until at last …
sentences.zh: ……而他每次上门出诊，都会顺手从她家里带走一件东西，直到最后……

sentences.en: … when he visited her for the last time, and the cure was complete, there was nothing left.
sentences.zh: ……当他最后一次来看诊、疗程完成时，家里已经什么都剩不下了。

sentences.en: When the Old Woman saw that the house was empty she refused to pay him his fee …
sentences.zh: 老妇见屋里空了，便拒付酬金……

sentences.en: … and, after repeated refusals on her part, he sued her before the magistrates for payment of her debt.
sentences.zh: ……她一再拒绝之后，医生便到地方官那里告她，索讨这笔欠款。

sentences.en: On being brought into court she was ready with her defence.
sentences.zh: 被带上公堂时，她早有辩解。

sentences.en: "The claimant," said she, "has stated the facts about our agreement correctly.
sentences.zh: 「原告，」她说，「把我们之间的约定讲得没错。

sentences.en: I undertook to pay him a fee if he cured me, and he, on his part, promised to charge nothing if he failed.
sentences.zh: 我承诺若治好便付酬金，而他那边则答应若治不好就不收分文。

sentences.en: Now, he says I am cured; but I say that I am blinder than ever, and I can prove what I say.
sentences.zh: 现在他说我治好了；可我说我比从前更瞎，而且我能证明我说的话。

sentences.en: When my eyes were bad I could at any rate see well enough to be aware that my house contained a certain amount of furniture and other …
sentences.zh: 我眼睛不好的时候，至少还能看清我家里有多少家具和别的……

sentences.en: … things; but now, when according to him I am cured, I am entirely unable to see anything there at all."
sentences.zh: 「……东西；可是如今，按他的说法我已痊愈，我却完全看不见家里有任何东西了。」

title: The Ass, the Fox, and the Lion
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Ass and a Fox went into partnership and sallied out to forage for food together.
sentences.zh: 一头驴和一只狐狸结成了搭伴，一起出去觅食。

sentences.en: They hadn't gone far before they saw a Lion coming their way, at which they were both dreadfully frightened.
sentences.zh: 没走多远，它们就看见一头狮子朝这边来，两个都吓坏了。

sentences.en: But the Fox thought he saw a way of saving his own skin …
sentences.zh: 可是狐狸觉得自己看到了一条保住性命的办法……

sentences.en: … and went boldly up to the Lion and whispered in his ear, "I'll manage that you shall get hold of the Ass without the trouble of …
sentences.zh: ……便壮着胆子走到狮子跟前，在他耳边低声说：「我能让您不必费事就抓住那头驴……」

sentences.en: … stalking him, if you'll promise to let me go free."
sentences.zh: 「……免去跟踪的麻烦，只要您答应放我一条生路。」

sentences.en: The Lion agreed to this, and the Fox then rejoined his companion and contrived before long to lead him by a hidden pit …
sentences.zh: 狮子答应了。狐狸于是回到伙伴身边，没多久就设法把它引到一个隐着的深坑旁……

sentences.en: … which some hunter had dug as a trap for wild animals, and into which he fell.
sentences.zh: ……那坑是哪个猎人挖来捕野兽的陷阱，驴掉了进去。

sentences.en: When the Lion saw that the Ass was safely caught and couldn't get away, it was to the Fox that he first turned his attention …
sentences.zh: 狮子见驴已被牢牢困住逃不掉了，便先转过头来对付狐狸……

sentences.en: … and he soon finished him off, and then at his leisure proceeded to feast upon the Ass.
sentences.zh: ……很快就结果了他，然后才不慌不忙地饱餐那头驴。

sentences.en: Betray a friend, and you'll often find you have ruined yourself.
sentences.zh: 背叛朋友的人，往往发现毁掉的是自己。
